title: Moi Moi
description: Steamed bean pudding: peeled black-eyed beans blended with peppers and onion, enriched with oil and crayfish, then steamed until silky and set.

image.alt: Cups of steamed orange moi moi with boiled egg in a steamer pot

equipment.name: Large heavy-bottomed pot with a tight lid
equipment.notes: A thin pot scorches the base

equipment.name: Heatproof ramekins, foil cups or moi moi leaves

steps.instruction: Soak the beans in plenty of water.

cues.texture: Skins wrinkle and slip when rubbed.

steps.instruction: Rub handfuls of beans between your palms to loosen the skins. Add water, let the skins float up and pour them off. Repeat until the beans are white.

cues.visual: Beans almost all white, with few dark eyes left.

steps.instruction: Blend the peeled beans with the tatashe, scotch bonnets, onion and about 250 ml water until very smooth.

cues.texture: Smooth, with no grit when rubbed between fingers.

steps.instruction: Pour into a bowl and whisk in the oil, crayfish, crumbled stock cubes and salt. Add warm water a little at a time until it pours like thick pancake batter.

cues.texture: Falls from the spoon in a thick ribbon.

image.alt: Oil being poured into moi moi batter while it is whisked

steps.instruction: Grease the ramekins, fill each about three-quarters full and push in a slice of egg.

image.alt: Moi moi batter being spooned into small round containers

steps.instruction: Stand the ramekins in a pot with boiling water a third of the way up their sides. Cover tightly and steam, topping up with boiling water if needed.
steps.completionNote: A skewer pushed into the centre comes out clean.
steps.safetyNote: Lift the lid away from you — the steam burns.

image.alt: Containers of moi moi with egg sitting in a steamer pot

steps.instruction: Turn off the heat and let them rest before turning out.

notes: Peeling is the slow part. Soaked beans can also be pulsed briefly in a blender with water to loosen skins.
Serve with jollof rice, pap (ogi) or custard, or on its own.
